footer.aboutText: This is a fun Navy-style aptitude quiz built around bearings, chart clues, signals, memory callbacks, safe decisions, and quick crew logic. It is for entertainment and self-challenge only. It is not an official Navy test, recruitment exam, military assessment, maritime credential, or training advice.

stageGroups.title: Deck Training
stageGroups.encouragement: You handled the starter checks. Now the harbour mission adds route choices, weather pressure, and details worth remembering.

questions.prompt: Deck training begins. If you are facing the bow, which side of the ship is port?
A patrol boat is heading north and turns right. Which direction is it heading now?
During briefing, the captain says the blue marker shows the safe channel. What does the blue marker mean in this drill?
Which tool is most useful for checking direction on a sea chart?
A signal lamp flashes code 3 during training. What does code 3 mean in this drill?
The launch leaves at 09:15 and the deck team has 30 minutes to get ready. When should the crew be ready?
Which sequence makes the most sense before leaving harbour?
choices: Cast off, check weather, brief crew
Check weather, brief crew, cast off
Brief crew, cast off, check weather
Cast off, brief crew, check weather

questions.prompt: During the same briefing, the captain says Harbour Gate B opens last. Which gate opens last?
A rescue boat must reach a marker before visibility drops. It covers 18 kilometres in 3 hours. What speed is it holding?
Quick trick check: what direction is directly opposite southeast?

stageGroups.title: Harbour Mission
stageGroups.encouragement: You got through the harbour run. The next round adds faster signals, route trade-offs, and decisions under pressure.

questions.prompt: The Harbour Mission starts at marker A2. The crew moves two columns right and one row up. Where are they now?
Visibility drops near the harbour mouth. What should matter most right away?
A tow line is attached and one route is shorter but rougher. Which choice is safest?
choices: Take the rough route to save time
Split the crew between both routes
Stop and drift with no plan
Take the calmer route and protect the tow

questions.prompt: A deck timer shows 12 minutes left. A safety drill takes 4 minutes and a line check takes 3 minutes. How much time remains?
A light sequence flashes red, white, red. What is the best crew response?
choices: Guess what it means and continue
Ignore it because the route is familiar
Log it and confirm the signal before acting

questions.prompt: The route moves from C3 to C6. What changed?
A weather report says wind is rising and spray is reducing visibility. Which message gets highest priority?
choices: Visibility is dropping on the route

questions.prompt: Which sequence is most sensible when a route suddenly looks uncertain?
choices: Speed up, ask later, check chart last
Keep going and hope the marker appears
Slow down, verify the chart, confirm with the crew

questions.prompt: The crew has 24 minutes before visibility worsens. A chart check takes 6 minutes and a signal check takes 6 minutes. They still need one final route check after that. What matters most?
choices: Whether there is still enough time to complete the checks before visibility drops
Whether the rope locker is tidy
Whether the boat looks faster from the dock

questions.prompt: A signal sheet says: A = slow approach, B = hold position, C = safe channel. The lamp flashes B while visibility drops. What should the crew do?
choices: Speed up before visibility gets worse
Hold position and confirm the next move
Switch channels without telling the crew
Ignore the lamp and trust the chart

stageGroups.title: Signal Pressure
stageGroups.encouragement: This is where the mission tightens. The final round brings back earlier clues when the pressure is highest.

questions.prompt: A warning lamp flashes twice, then stops. What is the smartest first move?
choices: Assume it was harmless and continue
Log it and confirm what the signal means

questions.prompt: A route through open water is quicker, but the sheltered route is steadier in worsening weather. Which choice is smarter?
choices: Take the quicker open-water route every time
Split the crew between both routes
Stop and wait with no plan

questions.prompt: Mission Control says the vessel is at D4 and must move one column right and one row down. Where does it end up?
A route update must include location, hazard, and next move. Which message does that best?
choices: We are somewhere near the marker
Visibility dropping near B6; slowing and switching to the marked safe channel
We may need to rethink things

questions.prompt: A deck team has 14 minutes left. A line reset takes 5 minutes and a signal check takes 4 minutes. How much time remains?
If only confirmed routes show a green light, and Route C has a green light, what can you safely conclude?
A crew member reports, “The marker looked wrong.” What is the smartest follow-up?
choices: Ask what exactly looked wrong and where
Ignore it because the route is familiar
Tell them to keep quiet until docking

questions.prompt: A vessel faces east, turns left, then turns left again. Which direction is it facing now?
The crew hears three updates at once: rising wind, a loose rope, and a missing mug. Which gets priority?
choices: The rising wind that affects the route

questions.prompt: Which sequence is smartest when a signal is unclear and the weather is worsening?
choices: Guess the signal, speed up, explain later
Confirm the signal, slow the approach, update the crew
Ignore the signal because weather matters more
Wait silently and hope the route clears

stageGroups.title: Final Command Check
stageGroups.encouragement: This is where most people fail. The final round mixes route memory, signal recall, and split-second command decisions.

questions.prompt: Earlier in the drill, what did the blue marker show?
Earlier, signal code 3 told the crew to do what?
Earlier in training, which harbour gate opened last?
Earlier in the mission, what did a green light show?
The blue marker showed the safe channel, and visibility is now poor. Which choice is safest?
choices: Ignore the marker and trust instinct
Wait for daylight with no message
Speed up before visibility gets worse
Follow the blue-marked channel at controlled speed

questions.prompt: A launch has 40 minutes before the tide changes, and the crossing takes 25 minutes. How much margin remains?
You are told: Alpha before Bravo, Bravo before Delta, Charlie after Delta. Which order fits?
Starting at B2, move one column left and two rows up. Where do you end?
Two updates arrive together: code 3 flashes, and the crew hears a meal-time reminder. Which one controls the next move?
Final command: the blue marker showed the safe channel, code 3 meant hold position, and Gate B opens last. In poor visibility with Gate B still closed, what should the crew do first?
choices: Hold position and wait for the safe channel to clear through Gate B
Rush the gate before the route changes
Ignore the marker and take the shortest line
Split the crew and try both routes at once
